title: What is stored for unknown sign-in names has a ceiling no flood raises, and its check fails only on a build that exceeds it
description: The sign-in flood check saw the unknown-name store 14 rows past its bound under CI load. The product promises a ceiling no flood raises; whether the build or the check is wrong is observed first.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first under CI's shape (2 CPUs, -count=20) and recorded in docs/testing.md with queue run 44986442604: rows per signin_* table before and after each of 10 successive floods of 20,000 names past the bound with 16 writers; which table the 116 and the 14 rows were in; whether the excess rises flood over flood
The rule holds: the count never rises from flood to flood, and during a flood is over the bound by no more than the sign-ins in flight

If the build meets the rule, the check is amended to assert it, and is shown to fail on a build that leaks one row per flood and on one with no cap. docs/access.md states the bound with its slack. Both cite D-050
If the build does not meet it, the product is fixed. A fix that would slow a sign-in measurably, or needs a lock across replicas, is briefed first
JS-145 criterion 8 still holds: no real account's count changes and no unknown name answers differently
The record gives BL-214's undershoot at the shipped bound, with no fix unless its promotion rule is met; BL-220 stays open
No retry, skip or raised timeout
notes: Builds beside JS-161 and never holds it, nor JS-041 or JS-157 (D-050). Merged c9f1807 (#251).
